hints.content:
$\displaystyle \lim_{x\to 7}f(x)$ represents the limit of $f$ as $x$ approaches $7$.

We see that $f(7)\approx -3$, but the $y$-values seem to approach a different value as the $x$-values approach $7$.

![The graph of function f has arrows pointing along the curve, down to the right and up to the left, respectively, to the open circle.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/ec688c99e0430d80615c08e439a9fb8d60205594)

The limit seems to be about halfway between $y=-7$ and $y=-6$.

![The graph of function f has a dashed horizontal line intersecting the open circle midway between y = negative 7 and y = negative 6.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/1639f88f411a30e52279867f5056ff42c9701ec6)

question.content:
The function $f$ is defined for all real numbers.

![Function f is graphed. The x-axis goes from negative 8 to 8. The graph consists of a curve and a closed circle. The curve starts in quadrant 3 and moves downward through an open circle at x = 7, midway between y = negative 6 and y = negative 7. The closed circle is plotted at x = 7, just below the grid line for y = negative 3.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/98106a199feac8e968c1ae862d2ea55ba48fdebf)

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 7}f(x)$ ?**
